papers.title: MNT-DeepSL: Median nerve tracking from carpal tunnel ultrasound images with deep similarity learning and analysis on continuous wrist motions
papers.abstract: Proposed MNT-DeepSL using deep similarity learning (Siamese-style tracking) to track median nerve trajectories in continuous wrist motion ultrasound videos, enabling kinematic biomarker extraction for CTS assessment.
papers.source_excerpt: Deep similarity learning tracker (MNT-DeepSL) for continuous median nerve trajectory analysis in dynamic carpal tunnel ultrasound.

papers.title: Accurate automated diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome using radiomics features with ultrasound images: A comparison with radiologists' assessment
papers.abstract: Extracted high-dimensional ultrasound radiomics features (texture, wavelets, histogram) from median nerve ROIs and trained machine learning classifiers (SVM, Random Forest) to diagnose CTS, outperforming subjective visual assessment by radiologists.
papers.source_excerpt: Ultrasound radiomics feature extraction coupled with ML classifiers exceeds radiologist diagnostic accuracy for CTS.

papers.title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Automated Diagnosis: A Motor vs. Sensory Nerve Conduction-Based Approach
papers.abstract: Compared automated CTS diagnosis and severity grading from raw motor vs. sensory nerve conduction signals using short-time Fourier transform (STFT) spectrograms with 2D CNNs and multilevel wavelet decomposition (MWD), achieving 94%–97.1% accuracy.
papers.source_excerpt: Time-frequency STFT spectrograms + 2D CNNs and wavelet decomposition on raw motor/sensory nerve conduction waveforms achieve 94-97.1% accuracy.

papers.title: Automatic Electrodiagnosis of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Applied machine learning classifiers (SVM, Decision Trees, Random Forests, k-NN, Neural Networks) to electrodiagnostic nerve conduction signals and extracted features for automated CTS detection and severity grading.
papers.source_excerpt: Automated electrodiagnosis of CTS from nerve conduction signals using classical machine learning classifiers.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Approach for Disease Severity Classification of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
papers.abstract: Evaluated multiple machine learning algorithms (Extreme Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, SVM, CNN) combining clinical, anthropometric, ultrasound CSA, and electrophysiological features to classify CTS severity into mild, moderate, and severe grades.
papers.source_excerpt: Random Forest / XGBoost severity classification of CTS integrating clinical, anthropometric, and diagnostic parameters.
